Emily / Sofia — here's the technical evaluation plan (compact, focused):

Run window: 21–22 Jul 2027. Two test teams: Redwood ops (runs), VertexMed to observe / provide sample prompts.

Test matrix (per deployment mode: Hosted, Dedicated, Private):
- Workloads:
  * Steady-state: 1k requests over 30 minutes, interp. arrival Poisson (mean RPS tuned to target concurrency).
  * Burst/stress: 10x spike windows (5 min) to validate autoscale + degradation behavior.
  * Long-run isolation: 3-hour run with synthetic noisy neighbors for Hosted to check variance.
- Concurrency points: 5, 20, 100 concurrent sessions (simulated clients with independent KV caches).
- Payload: average prompt tokens=120, max tokens=1024 (generation tail tests).

Metrics we will capture (per request):
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT)
- Latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) for first token and end-to-end generation
- Throughput (tokens/sec per model instance) and aggregate
- CPU/GPU utilization, memory, KV cache hit ratio
- Autoscale events: time-to-scale-up, replacement/queueing indicators
- Error rates and graceful-fallback events (model switch / reduced sampling)

Acceptance criteria (proposed — can be tuned):
- p95 end-to-end generation under target concurrency (20): <= 300ms for Dedicated, <= 450ms for Hosted, <= 250ms for Private
- TTFT p95: <= 120ms Dedicated, <= 200ms Hosted, <= 100ms Private
- No sustained error spikes >0.5% during steady-state
- Throughput: sustained token/sec within 10% of the baseline profile for Dedicated/Private; Hosted should be within 15% when not autoscaling

Instrumentation & reproducibility:
- We'll run the open-source harness (link) and provide run scripts + raw traces.
- Produce a one-page executive summary and a full benchmark report (CSV + PDF).

Run commands & links:
- Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness
- Example run: ./run_bench --mode hosted --clients 20 --duration 30m --prompts sample_prompts.json

I'll coordinate with Redwood infra to provision Dedicated capacity for the run and request VertexMed sandbox creds for the Private test.

Marcus Lin
Performance Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: performance acceptance + hosting comparison — results and next steps

Emily — attaching the full report and a one-page summary. Key findings below (executive summary):

Summary (measured across the representative prompt set):
- Hosted:
  * p50 end-to-end: 85ms 
  * p95: 420ms (notable variance during noisy-neighbor windows)
  * p99: 1.2s (spikes during autoscale events)
  * TTFT p95: 210ms
  * Throughput (aggregate tokens/sec): ~1,150
  * Observations: good baseline latency for light concurrency; when concurrency >=100 or during noisy neighbor injection we saw increased p95 and p99. Autoscale reacted but introduced brief higher p99 spikes during warmup.

- Dedicated (provisioned GPU pool):
  * p50: 60ms
  * p95: 170ms
  * p99: 420ms
  * TTFT p95: 95ms
  * Throughput: ~2,200 tokens/sec per cluster (steady)
  * Observations: stable tail latency, predictable throughput. Autoscaling (configured) scaled predictably on 10x bursts with ~45s median time-to-scale-up.

- Private (customer-managed VPC on comparable infra):
  * p50: 55ms
  * p95: 150ms
  * p99: 380ms
  * TTFT p95: 80ms
  * Throughput: ~2,500 tokens/sec (limited by customer's per-node config in this run)
  * Observations: most consistent latency; limited by node sizing — needs additional capacity for higher sustained concurrency.

Autoscaling & isolation notes:
- Hosted showed the highest variability under synthetic noisy neighbors; fallback policies worked (short-lived model switch) but increased p99 while warmup occurred.
- Dedicated provided the best balance of predictability and cost (when reserved).
- Private gave the tightest tail latencies but will require explicit capacity planning (no autoscale if customer does not configure it).

Acceptance gating (per VertexMed procurement appendix):
- Gate 1 (performance): p95 end-to-end <= 300ms on Dedicated or Private; Hosted acceptable if within 450ms and documented autoscale behavior.
- Gate 2 (stability): sustained error rate <0.5% over a 30-minute steady-state window and no more than two >10% p95 regressions during spike tests.
- Gate 3 (TTFT): p95 <= 120ms for Dedicated/Private.

Deliverables attached: benchmark-report-hosted-dedicated-private-20270722.pdf (full results + CSVs inside), vm_vertexmed_map_v1.xlsx (updated), load-scripts.tar.gz (run artifacts).

Next steps we recommend:
- VertexMed sign-off on gating thresholds (proposed above).
- If closing on Dedicated: agree committed capacity and an autoscale cushion for bursts.
- If Private: confirm node sizing for target concurrency (we recommend +20% headroom).

If you want, Marcus can walk through the PDF in a 30-minute call.

Best,
Sofia
